description: I am an independent young developer and creative problem-solver with an interest in space exploration, science, and game development. I enjoy turning complex ideas into interactive experiences. I created Mission Forge, an educational space mission design game inspired by NASA Space Apps challenges. I am motivated, resourceful, curious, and eager to learn, build projects, and contribute my ideas independently.
summary:
Mission Forge: Space Mission Design Game

Mission Forge is an educational space mission design game inspired by NASA's Space Mission Design Game challenge. It allows players to experience the process of planning a space mission by making important decisions about destinations, objectives, launch vehicles, scientific instruments, power systems, communications, budgets, and mission duration.

Through an interactive interface, players build and evaluate their own fictional missions while balancing scientific goals, technical requirements, and available resources. The game includes live mission checks, a six-phase mission simulation, scoring, a mission debrief, and an event log to help players understand the results of their decisions. Players can also generate a JSON mission report and consult an integrated handbook for guidance.

The goal of Mission Forge is to make space mission planning more accessible, engaging, and understandable through interactive learning. It encourages creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and an appreciation of the challenges involved in exploring space.
details: Mission Forge – Space Mission Design Game Mission Forge is an interactive educational game that allows users to design and simulate their own fictional space missions. Players choose a mission destination and scientific objective, then make important decisions about launch vehicles, scientific instruments, power systems, communications, budget, and mission duration. The game evaluates these choices through live mission checks and a six-phase simulation, followed by a score, mission debrief, and event log. The project benefits students, space enthusiasts, and beginners by making complex space mission planning easier to understand through hands-on learning. Its intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and help users appreciate the challenges involved in planning real-world missions. Mission Forge was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It does not require specialized hardware or external software installations; users can run it in a modern web browser. Its creativity comes from combining game mechanics with educational mission planning. Instead of simply presenting information, it lets users experiment with different mission designs and see how their decisions affect outcomes. Key factors considered during development included scientific objectives, technical compatibility, available resources, budget limits, mission duration, communication needs, and educational accessibility. The project uses fictional educational values to demonstrate mission-planning concepts.
